C_mac_screen.say: Sorry it's acting up. What exactly is the screen doing, for example flickering, lines across it, going dark, or showing odd colors? That tells me whether this is something safe to check yourself or something for a repair shop.

whether there is physical damage or liquid exposure

C_mac_screen.user: only the external monitor, the laptop screen is fine
C_mac_screen.say: Good to know the laptop screen is fine, that points toward the external monitor, its cable, or the connection rather than the Mac itself. What is the external monitor actually doing, for example flickering, going black, showing lines, wrong colors, or the wrong resolution? That decides which checks make sense.
critical_unknowns: how the monitor is connected (cable or adapter type)
facts: Mac laptop with an external monitor
Problem limited to external monitor; built-in laptop screen works normally
External display issue, likely cable, adapter, port or display settings

STEP_explain.question: How do these round metal locks work, and how far should I turn them?
STEP_explain.answer: Each round metal lock is a cam lock. It sits in the round hole in the panel face and grabs the head of the cam bolt you screwed into the matching edge earlier. Press cam lock 103430 into each hole shown, with its open side facing the bolt so the bolt head can slide in. Then turn it with a screwdriver. The guide says a quarter turn, and that pulls the panels snugly together. Don't force it past where it firmly stops. Use only 103430 here. The guide crosses out cam lock 110126 for this step.
